title: Checkpointed delta output and evented SDK ergonomics (PRD draft)
content:
Summary
This PRD proposes a new output surface and companion SDK ergonomics for the Hosted API: a checkpointed, delta-oriented response protocol with explicit event boundaries and resume semantics. The goal is to give client applications low-latency partial results, robust resume/rewind for unreliable networks or client restarts, and a simple, cross-platform SDK surface that maps to common app patterns (chat, editors, tool-calls, and offline sync).

Problem statement
- Current incremental-output modes provide raw token streams or chunked partial responses, but lack consistent, minimal primitives for:
  - check-pointing meaningful progress (so clients can resume without re-generation)
  - expressing structured deltas (small JSON patches or typed frames) in an ergonomic way
  - signaling client-side backpressure and transient offline sync semantics
- App teams build ad-hoc wrappers around streaming tokens which leads to duplication, bugs around replay/resume, and fragile tool integrations.

Goals
- Define a server-side frame format (text+control frames) that encodes typed deltas and checkpoint markers.
- Provide resume semantics at the frame level so clients can reconnect and continue without full re-generation when safe.
- Surface a small SDK abstraction that:
  - exposes evented callbacks for delta frames, checkpoints, and lifecycle events
  - exposes an async iterator/observable for progressive UI flows
  - exposes deterministic replay hooks for local offline reconcilers
- Make rollout incremental: start with WebSocket/HTTP chunked-transfer streaming and a fallback long-polling mode.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not specify a complete typed schema for every possible tool output (we recommend a small core set + extension points).
- Not targeting binary frames or custom wire protocols beyond HTTP/1 chunked and WebSocket v13.

User stories
- Chat app: show partial message content as the model composes; if a customer reloads the tab mid-response, reconnect and resume from the last checkpoint.
- Document assistant: apply typed deltas (replace, insert, annotate) as they arrive so we can render and highlight edits progressively.
- Tool-hybrid flow: stream structured tool-call intents separately from text synthesis (so UI can fetch external data while completion continues).

Design overview
1) Frame types (high-level)
  - DATA_DELTA: granular, typed delta that contains a minimal change payload (JSON string).
  - CHECKPOINT: stable marker indicating a point where the server can guarantee idempotent resume from this point (contains checkpoint_id).
  - METADATA: initial and final metadata frames (model, temperature, approx token counts, costs).
  - EVENT: lifecycle events (tool_call_started, tool_call_result, error_detail).
  - HEARTBEAT: optional keepalive.

2) Wire format (text-based, newline-delimited)
Use newline-delimited JSON frames. Each line is a small JSON object with two required keys: type and seq. Example frame stream (pseudo):

{"type":"METADATA","seq":0,"body":{"model":"redwood-v2","seed":123}}
{"type":"DATA_DELTA","seq":1,"body":{"deltaType":"insert","path":["document","blocks",3],"content":"Hello"}}
{"type":"DATA_DELTA","seq":2,"body":{"deltaType":"insert","path":["document","blocks",4],"content":"World"}}
{"type":"CHECKPOINT","seq":3,"body":{"checkpoint_id":"cp_20260220_0001","cursor_token":"sCk..."}}

Notes: body is a stringified JSON object but framed as text. Clients should stream-parse line-by-line. The seq field is monotonically increasing and used for resume checks.

3) Resume semantics
- Clients store the last persisted CHECKPOINT (checkpoint_id + seq) in local storage or server-side session.
- On reconnect, client sends resume_hint: {last_checkpoint_id, last_seq}.
- Server will attempt one of:
  - confirm resume possible (return ACK_RESUME and continue streaming from server-internal point),
  - perform lightweight delta replay by re-emitting frames since last_seq (when supported), or
  - fallback to a new generation (return START_NEW_GENERATION) when resume can't be guaranteed.
- Resume is best-effort; clients must handle the START_NEW_GENERATION case by reconciling a short UI flicker or asking user confirmation depending on app.

4) Backpressure & client signals
- Clients can send a small control channel (WS sub-protocol or a trailing HTTP request) with signals: BUFFER_STATUS, CLIENT_DEMAND (tokens wanted), and CANCEL_REASON.
- Server respects client demand for adaptive batching where possible; minimal SLO guarantees still apply (server may not stop generation mid-token to satisfy demand).

5) Structured tool boundaries
- Tool-invocation semantics are expressed as EVENT frames. Example: EVENT(tool_call_started, {tool: "http_fetch", inputs: {...}}) followed by DATA_DELTA frames with the tool results annotated as deltaType:"tool_result".
- Tool frames include an opaque tool_call_id so clients can correlate partial tool outputs and display progress.

SDK ergonomics proposal (surface)
- JavaScript/TypeScript SDK (reference):
  - connect(request): returns an object with: on('delta', cb), on('checkpoint', cb), on('event', cb), on('done', cb), close(), resume(resume_hint).
  - streamAsyncIterator(request): async iterable yielding {type, seq, body} for frameworks that prefer iterator patterns (React Suspense, SSG previews).
  - convenience: applyDeltaToModel(state, delta) helper that knows common deltaTypes (insert, replace, annotate) and returns new state.
- Mobile (iOS/Android) SDKs mirror the evented callbacks and expose a small StateApplier utility implemented natively.
- Default behavior: SDK persists last CHECKPOINT to a configurable storage layer (localStorage for web, secure local DB for mobile). Persisted data is small (checkpoint_id, seq, metadata).

Observability & telemetry
- Per-request telemetry fields: frames_emitted, last_checkpoint_seq, resume_attempts, resume_success, mean_delta_size_bytes, client_disconnects.
- Logs should include mapping from checkpoint_id -> server-internal retention window.
- SLO/alerting: spike in START_NEW_GENERATION outcomes during resumes should trigger alert (possible data loss or storage pressure).

Security & privacy considerations
- Checkpoint payloads should avoid persisting sensitive user content in shared browser storage by default when request includes privacy_sensitive flag; in that case SDK asks app to provide a server-side session token to resume instead of local checkpoints.
- Tool-call events must not leak secrets; tool inputs flagged secret should be redacted from DATA_DELTA frames and only indicated via event metadata.

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (prototype): 1 month — server prototype behind feature flag, JS SDK prototype, internal dogfood for editor/chat teams.
- Phase 1 (canary): 6% of production traffic — enable for a small set of tenants with supportive SDK versions; gather resume_success metrics and UI-replay telemetry.
- Phase 2 (expand): 25% — add native mobile SDK and docs; introduce long-poll fallback.
- Phase 3 (general availability): 100% — SDKs stable, promote defaults in new console routes.

API backward compatibility
- Default endpoints remain unchanged; new streaming endpoint is opt-in via header X-Redwood-Output-Mode: checkpointed-delta.
- For REST chunked responses we emit the same newline-delimited frames; for non-streaming clients we provide an endpoint that returns final merged content plus a last_checkpoint id for possible later resume (if server supports it).

Open questions
- How long do we retain server-side data needed to resume? (tradeoff between storage cost and UX)
- Should checkpoints be client-only (opaque cursor returned) or server-verifiable (signed tokens)?
- How to best surface partial billing estimates for in-progress responses?
- Do we allow application-defined deltaType extensions in the public SDK or require a gated plugin model?

Next steps / action items
- Product: finalize minimal set of deltaType schemas and wire-format fields (Rohit).
- Infra: prototype checkpoint persistence with retention policy knob (SLO: resume latency < 200ms) (Miles).
- Eng: implement JS SDK prototype and dogfood with chat/editor teams (Sofia).
- Draft public docs and migration guide for SDK users.

Appendix: example client flow (web, pseudo)
1) client calls connect(request). SDK opens WS.
2) server emits METADATA -> DATA_DELTA* -> CHECKPOINT frames as generation proceeds. SDK calls on('delta', cb) for UI updates.
3) client persists last CHECKPOINT after receiving it.
4) network disconnect. User reloads.
5) client calls resume({last_checkpoint_id, last_seq}). Server returns ACK_RESUME and replays frames since last_seq or continues generation.

References
- internal RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/72
- linear ticket: https://linear.redwood/ISSUE-1123

Notes to reviewers
- This is a draft focused on practical client ergonomics and low-latency UX. I'm intentionally keeping the initial delta schema small to avoid overfitting. Please comment on resume retention defaults and SDK storage choices.
